text:
Judd Caulfield took the long road: a fifth-round pick by Pittsburgh in 2019, college hockey at North Dakota, a full AHL season in San Diego, and now his first NHL games at 25. He has made them loud. His 75 hits in 21 games is a lot for anyone, never mind a winger playing about 14 minutes a night.

The scoring has come too, with 11 points, four on the power play. His last goal came in a two-goal night against Ottawa on Nov. 1, and he has gone nine games without one since, on 2.7 expected goals. That drought looks like bad finishing rather than a dried-up role: his chances per 60 minutes are above the typical forward's, and he's getting nearly three more minutes a night than he was.

At five on five, the Ducks are a bit under water with him on, about even with how they do without him. He doesn't shoot hard, so his goals come from close. The test now is whether his ice time holds while he waits for the puck to go in.
headline: Caulfield, 25, hitting everything in Anaheim
